tier_reason: doc/results.pdf (first-party, 5 pages) compares HYLU 20260331 with Intel MKL PARDISO 2025.3 on 37 SuiteSparse matrices and states CPU (Xeon Gold 6130), compilers (gcc 13.3.0 test code, gcc 8.5.0 library) and 16 threads, but no flags, no PARDISO settings and no public benchmark harness (demo/ only solves sample matrices); the library is binary-only and the arXiv preprint is not peer-reviewed as far as seen, so C.

corrections.license: None stated: no LICENSE file, and the README, include/hylu.h and doc/ug_en.pdf give no terms; prebuilt binaries only (unlike CKTSO, no license key file is required)
corrections.caveats: First-party evidence only: README and doc/results.pdf by the author, plus the author's arXiv preprint 2509.07690 (not opened; arXiv is unreachable here, and no copy of the paper is checked into the repo: doc/ holds only results.pdf, ug_cn.pdf and ug_en.pdf). A WebSearch snippet of the preprint abstract gives older figures: 34 SuiteSparse matrices, numerical factorization 1.95X (one-time) and 2.40X (repeated) faster than MKL PARDISO, versus 2.36X and 2.90X on 37 matrices in results.pdf (version 20260331). No benchmark code is public (demo/ only builds examples with gcc -O3 -std=gnu11 and solves sample .mtx files), compiler flags for the timed builds and the MKL PARDISO settings (ordering, iparm) are not stated, and all results are 16-thread wall time on one Xeon Gold 6130 with no sequential numbers. No license file or terms anywhere, and only binaries are provided (Linux .so built for CentOS 7 and Windows DLLs, MKL or OpenBLAS variants, x64 with AVX2/FMA), so it can be neither audited nor copied; usability is reference and has_code is false. Baseline is Intel MKL PARDISO, not SuiteSparse, Eigen sparse or PETSc. Per-matrix charts in results.pdf (read visually, approximate): in one-time total time HYLU is slower than PARDISO on af_shell10 (about 0.8x) and roughly even on CurlCurl_4 and a few others, while off-scale wins on ASIC_680k, ASIC_680ks, circuit5M and nlpkkt80, where PARDISO creates huge fill-in, lift the geometric mean; forward-backward substitution is slower on most matrices. The residual chart shows HYLU relative residuals near or above 1 on CurlCurl_2, CurlCurl_4 and dgreen (PARDISO worse still) and about 0.1 on nv2, so those timings come from runs that did not produce accurate solutions; the text acknowledges only Hamrle3. The matrix set is limited to 37 large SuiteSparse matrices (n from 525,825 to 5,558,326), and results.pdf (created 2026-04-01) uses version 20260331 while the latest is 20260930. Repo history runs from 2025-09-12 (initial release) to 2026-09-30 (39 commits). A sibling project by the same author, CKTSO, is already catalogued (https://github.com/chenxm1986/cktso); HYLU is a separate general-purpose solver, not a duplicate.

notes: All claimed numbers (1.70X, 2.36X, 1.48X, 18% slower FBS, 2.90X, 2.53X, 20% slower, order-of-magnitude accuracy) appear verbatim in doc/results.pdf text. No paper PDF is checked into the repo (unlike CKTSO's doc/tcad.pdf), so no B retier is possible; shortcoming worth recording: per the residual chart, several timed matrices (CurlCurl_2, CurlCurl_4, dgreen) were not solved accurately by either solver, and the geometric mean is lifted by four matrices where PARDISO fills in pathologically.
